title: A whole picture can hold too tightly

captions.energy: Connecting parts within a shared meaning

meaning: Comparing examples can help you see the whole, although emotional attachment to a complete explanation may obscure a question that remains open.
text: An explanation can be especially appealing when everything seems to have found a place within it. The Empress in the physical position of Ajna suggests creating visible material and comparing different examples. The World in energy supports the wish to see the whole and connect parts of experience within a meaningful picture. The Devil in emotions describes attachment to the version you have found: you enjoy returning to it and find its limits difficult to acknowledge. Interest in the subject can leave room for an unclear detail beside satisfaction in a shared account.

For example, after a film you draw a diagram of relationships between characters. Several actions connect within a persuasive story, but one scene remains unexplained. **A whole picture stays alive when its beauty leaves a question visible.** You can notice why the account fascinates you both and look again at the awkward scene. The visible material then helps deepen understanding. Enjoying the discovery remains possible although an unfinished edge remains available for another reading.

The difficulty is fitting every new point into a favourite structure so that it never changes. You appear to be assembling the whole while emotionally protecting a finished answer. Your wish to connect experience remains constructive when connections can be reconsidered. The picture may become less smooth and more meaningful while preserving the value of what you have already seen together.
